title: the ladder bake-off — per-channel warped quantizers fitted on family 7's training pentads and scored on held-out ones
comparability_note: Every scheme's held-out cross-entropy is computed on ONE COMMON FINE PARTITION E per channel — the 4,096 equal-probability quantiles of that channel's fit sample, clipped to [q0.0005, q0.9995], deduplicated (the tensor stores float16, so quantiles can coincide), plus two open end cells. A ladder's probability for a fine cell is its bin mass pi_k spread uniformly in x and intersected with the cell; the Gaussian and the Gaussian mixture give the difference of their cumulative distribution across the cell. This is the ONLY way a discrete quantizer and a continuous density are comparable at all; a cross-entropy computed any other way is not comparable and its number means nothing.
regulariser_note: Every scheme (ladders and baselines alike) is mixed with a uniform-over-fine-cells escape of weight 1e-06 before the cross-entropy is taken, so that a scheme which gives some cell zero mass scores a large finite number rather than infinity. The mixture is identical for every scheme, so comparisons are unaffected; the 'uniform_cells' row is that escape distribution on its own.
units_note: The tensor stores z-scored values (docs/FAMILY7_DATA_HANDOVER.md section 4). Warps, partitions and cross-entropies are computed in stored units — cross-entropy over a common partition is a discrete quantity and is unit-free — and every RMSE and quantization floor is multiplied by that channel's sd from norm_<group> so it is reported in the channel's own physical unit.

sampling.note: Training years: bin opening year <= 2020 and not in {2009, 2017, 2023}. Held-out years: {2009, 2017, 2023}.
sampling.seasonal_note: The fit pairs are spread evenly over the whole ordered list of training candidate pairs rather than pinned inside each year, so the sampling phase precesses through the calendar; the two histograms above are the check that it did.

masks.tail: cells where cur_speed is in its top 1 % on that bin; applied to every g025 channel, mapped to the containing 1 deg cell for g100, not applied to rg100
masks.rapid_note: row 466 = 26.5 N, columns 400-668 = 80 W to 13 W on the 0.25 deg grid, and the containing 1 deg cells for g100 and rg100

F1_alpha1_vs_alpha0_heldout_nats.question: Does alpha = 1 (equal-probability bins) beat alpha = 0 (uniform bins) on held-out nats by more than the channel-to-channel spread of that difference? If not, the quantile idea does not survive its own data.

F2_conditional_entropy_flat_in_alpha.question: Is the coarse digit's conditional entropy H(d1(t+1)|d1(t)) flat in alpha at K1 = 64? If it is, section 4 of the plan is void and alpha = 1 is taken on the class-balance argument.
F2_conditional_entropy_flat_in_alpha.criterion: declared flat if the median across channels of the range across alpha is below 2 % of log(64) = 0.0832 nats (a threshold chosen here, stated so it can be disagreed with)
F2_conditional_entropy_flat_in_alpha.caveat: A lower conditional entropy at a small alpha is partly free: a ladder that ignores the density also carries less information, so its digit has a lower MARGINAL entropy too. The fraction H(next|now)/H(now) — how much of what the digit says survives a pentad — is the version of the question that cannot be won by saying less.

F3_tail_rmse_cur_speed.question: Is alpha = 1's reconstruction RMSE on the top 1 % of cur_speed worse than alpha = 1/3's by more than the alpha = 1/3 value itself? If so, tails decide and alpha = 1/3 is taken regardless of the nats column.

F4_depth2_vs_depth1_matched.question: At matched piece count (depth 2 with K1 = 64 and K2 = 64, i.e. 4,096 pieces, against depth 1 with K1 = 4,096), do the held-out nats agree to within 1 %? If not, the whitening argument of section 1.2 is wrong somewhere, or the implementation is at fault.
